cohort: The study included 5,401 non-pregnant women aged 20 years or older from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005-2014.
finding: Higher parity and an increased frequency of vaginal deliveries were significantly associated with a higher prevalence of depression among women.
mod_finding: An increased frequency of vaginal deliveries was associated with a higher prevalence of depression (OR: 1.12), and women with four or more cesarean deliveries had a 2.03 times higher prevalence of depression compared to those with no cesarean deliveries.
